To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the blood pressure screening program was effective in identifying a substantial number of previously undiagnosed hypertensives and that a high proportion of these patients were treated and had their hypertension controlled.
the MBP has identified a large group of hypertensives, and has provided them with treatment and control.
65% of private patients and 82% of clinic patients referred for hypertension control by the MBP have achieved blood pressure levels below 140/90 mm Hg.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the epidemiology of hypertension and with the evaluation of the efficacy of the community screening program.
developing methods to identify and treat hypertensives in the community and with the evaluation of the effectiveness of such methods.
developing methods for the detection of hypertension and with the evaluation of methods to control hypertension.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MBP has had a major impact on hypertension control in Milwaukee.
the MBP has been effective in identifying hypertensive patients and in initiating antihypertensives drugs in a majority of them, but that the results of treatment have been less than optimal.
the program has been able to identify a large number of hypertensive patients who have been confirmed by the referring physicians and who are being treated with appropriate antihypertensives.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a community based screening program can identify a substantial number of hypertensives, that most of these patients are treated, that most of them receive antihypertensives, and that a large percentage are controlled.
community blood pressure screening is feasible, that a high proportion of hypertensives can be identified and that a high proportion can be controlled by the use of antihypertensives.
a community screening program can detect hypertensive patients and can be followed up by a medical school affiliated community hypertension clinic.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a community blood pressure program can be an effective tool to identify and treat patients with hypertension.
community screening can be a useful tool in the identification of hypertensives who are at risk for complications of hypertension.
the MBP has provided an efficient method to identify hypertensives in a large community and to provide follow-up care in the private practice or the clinic setting.
